links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses to voice disorder questions (FRES, GFSL, Dale-Chall)
links.effect: Time slot 1 mean FRES 37.08, GFSL 15.76, D-CS 10.05; time slot 2 FRES 45.09, GFSL 15.04, D-CS 9.26, indicating high reading complexity for a general audience.
links.quote: The average scores for FRES, GFSL, D-CS, words count, sentence count, words per sentence, and characters per word at time slot 1 were 37.08, 15.76, 10.05, 117.53, 6.90, 17.48, and 5.47, respectively, indicating a high level of reading complexity for a general audience.

links.outcome: Reading level of chatbot responses relative to general public readers
links.effect: Mean FRES 37.08 and GFSL 15.76 at time 1; 45.09 and 15.04 at time 2, still complex, though somewhat improved in the newer model.
links.quote: The average scores for FRES, GFSL, D-CS, words count, sentence count, words per sentence, and characters per word at time slot 1 were 37.08, 15.76, 10.05, 117.53, 6.90, 17.48, and 5.47, respectively, indicating a high level of reading complexity for a general audience.

links.outcome: Accuracy, harm, and consensus alignment of ChatGPT answers rated by authors
links.effect: 91.7% free from inaccurate or inappropriate content; 92.5% harmless; 80% consistent with consensus; so about 8% inaccurate and 20% inconsistent with consensus.
links.quote: Most generated responses (91.7%) were free from inaccurate or inappropriate content; 92.5% were rated as harmless, and 80% were consistent with the consensus.

screen.reason: Evaluates the performance, accuracy, harm, and readability of ChatGPT (GPT-4o mini) responses to patient inquiries on voice disorders across two time points without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
